observedBehavior: The local Next proxy buffers the request before the route. When the body exceeds its configured per-request buffer limit, it logs a warning and continues with only the first N bytes available.
reasoning: The Next buffer must exceed the largest application cap so any clipped body still reaches the application reader with more than 6 MiB and is rejected. Valid 10,000-part JSON with 200 visible ETag characters requiring escaping is 4,299,010 bytes and fits the 6 MiB application cap.

before.nextWarning: Only the first 10MB will be available
before.result: Next truncated the request below the temporary 13 MiB reader limit; the partial form parsed and the route redirected for its absent token instead of rejecting the oversized request.

after.nextWarning: Only the first 10MB will be available
after.result: The truncated body still exceeded the 6 MiB reader limit and was rejected before FormData parsing.

productionBuildWithConfigured7MiBProxyLi.nextWarning: Only the first 7MB will be available

temporaryChanges: Route limit values were changed only in the local worktree to compare behavior, then restored before commit. No production container, database, registry, DNS, or external proxy was accessed.
scopeLimitations: The before/after route experiments used Next dev mode; the 7 MiB configuration check used a local optimized Next production server.
The direct tests did not include Cloudflare or another external reverse proxy.
The optimized-server request used the existing 16 KiB public route cap; no authenticated 6 MiB upload was sent.
